title: 問路與搭地鐵
scene: 你在陌生城市要去中央車站，攔住一個路人問路。要問怎麼搭、在哪搭、要不要轉車、票多少錢、車程多久、從哪個出口出來。

lines.en: Excuse me, how do I get to Central Station?
lines.zh: 不好意思，請問中央車站怎麼去？

lines.en: You can take the blue line. It's three stops.
lines.zh: 你可以搭藍線，三站就到。

lines.en: Go down these stairs and follow the signs.
lines.zh: 從這個樓梯下去，照指標走。

lines.en: How much is a single ticket?
Two fifty. You can buy it at the machine.
It does, but it doesn't give change.
Good to know. How long does it take?
And which exit should I use?
Exit B. It comes out right at the square.
lines.zh: B 出口，出來就是廣場。

lines.en: No problem. Have a good one.

vocab.example_en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
vocab.example_zh: 不好意思，這位子有人嗎？

vocab.example_en: How do I get to the airport?
It's only two stops from here.
You have to transfer at the next station.
Take Exit B and turn right.
vocab.example_zh: 走 B 出口然後右轉。

tips: 問路一定要用 Excuse me 開頭。直接問 How do I get to… 會顯得很沒禮貌，這在國外比想像中嚴重。
「三站」用 stop 不是 station —— station 指的是車站那棟建築，stop 才是計算站數的單位。
change 在這裡是「找零」不是「改變」。這是台灣人最常誤會的一字多義，聽到 no change 是說不找零。
Two fifty 就是 $2.50，母語人士不會唸 two point five dollars。價格幾乎都用這種「整數＋分」的唸法。
Have a good one. 是很口語的道別，等於 Have a nice day。聽到不用想太多，回 You too. 就好。
